quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the street.
questions.explanation: You must drive with great care when children are nearby. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road gradually.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently brake and slowly steer back onto the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake and slowly steer back onto the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement and gently apply the brakes to slow down. Once you are at a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light warns of a dangerous intersection. Treat it the same way you would treat a stop sign.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers make many decisions for every mile driven. You must focus fully on driving. Any other activity can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: You must stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle away from traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must not pass another vehicle.
You may pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You may pass if you know the road ahead.
You may pass only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must not pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white rectangles with black words. You must follow all instructions on regulatory signs. This sign means no passing is allowed.

questions.question: Failure to yield the right-of-way is the leading cause of accidents in Nevada.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way laws help traffic flow through intersections safely. They require courtesy, common sense, and cooperation. Not yielding the right-of-way causes the most accidents in Nevada.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams bounce off the fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: How can you avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving next to them and do not follow too closely behind them.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulders to check these areas.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians can safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces your ability to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Speed up and drive past the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to scare them away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection, even if you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Call 911 if anyone is injured. Report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or property damage over $1,000.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes:

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting. The road splits into two one-way lanes separated by a divider. Stay to the right.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ can cause a crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel is a distraction.

questions.question: If someone has drunk alcohol, what will help them overcome it?
questions.explanation: Only time allows the body to overcome the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: When pulled over by police, you should immediately exit your vehicle and walk to the officer's car.
questions.explanation: Stay in your vehicle with both hands visible on the steering wheel when stopped by police.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful where children are present. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way in crosswalks.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, near pedestrians or hazards, and on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, ____ has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. Once the lead vehicle enters an intersection, other vehicles in the procession can follow through, even if traffic signals say to stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two lanes of traffic are about to become one lane.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
The driver who arrives last has the right-of-way.
One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: All four directions must stop at a four-way stop. The first vehicle to arrive goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: It starts raining while you are driving. You should:

options.text: Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Slow down when rain reduces visibility. Turn on your headlights. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until the rain lets up.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and keep any passengers' hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and proceed with caution near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog. Be ready to stop to prevent injury.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on a yellow background. They alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready to respond to a yellow or red light.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for road conditions

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other drivers are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws as if the area is not under construction.

questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and drive carefully when a sign, flagger, or police officer directs you to do so. Not following these instructions is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired is a serious traffic safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or taking other drugs. Drinking and driving puts you and everyone on the road at risk.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean:

options.text: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
Passing is permitted from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You may only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter riders when the opposite lane is clear and safe.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving up or down:

options.text: As long as an approaching train is not too close.
If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.
If you first look carefully in both directions.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not drive until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: As you near an intersection, the traffic light turns from green to yellow. You should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Apply the brakes sharply to stop.
Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be prepared to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light means the light will soon turn red. Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning more difficult. They also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
When passing, wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.explanation: Always signal at least 100 feet before passing. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.

questions.question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see at night, even with lights and reflectors. Drivers and cyclists must be extra careful at night to prevent accidents.

questions.question: A driver taking a non-prescription drug should:

options.text: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medications can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings about side effects. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure whether you can safely drive while taking a medication.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another way to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or going fast enough to be dangerous, you cannot cross. This rule applies even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: You do not need to leave as much distance when following a motorcycle as when following a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions. You should stay three to four seconds behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to move in an emergency.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol?

options.text: They always know the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Before you move into the other lane, quickly turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a four-way intersection is coming.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted?
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at an intersection. A crosswalk is any place where two streets meet, whether marked or unmarked.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign tells drivers a lane is ending and they should prepare for traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the narrow bridge ahead.
The bridge ahead has one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead can fit only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a bridge may be too narrow to safely pass a truck, and drivers should be careful.
